This is arguably the most dishonest definition of socialism that I have ever seen, even worse than that used by some conservatives who think Medicare is "socialism." Socialism is state ownership of the means of production, not any regulation of it. From Merriam-Webster:

a way of organizing a society in which major industries are owned and controlled by the government rather than by individual people and companies [emphasis added]

Despite searching, I cannot find any dictionary that uses the definition proposed in this video. Also, one only has to ponder it for a moment to realize how ridiculous it is. According to this video, literally any regulation of an economy is socialism, meaning that anything other than Anarchism/Anarcho-Capitalism is socialism. Defining any term that broadly renders it meaningless.

Different websites and sources seem to define socialism differently, I'll give you that much. This seems to be how the website for the World Socialist Movement defines it:

Central to the meaning of socialism is common ownership. This means the resources of the world being owned in common by the entire global population. But does it really make sense for everybody to own everything in common? Of course, some goods tend to be for personal consumption, rather than to share—clothes, for example. People 'owning' certain personal possessions does not contradict the principle of a society based upon common ownership. In practice, common ownership will mean everybody having the right to participate in decisions on how global resources will be used. It means nobody being able to take personal control of resources, beyond their own personal possessions.

But even that website centers on ownership as the key concept, simply pointing out that total control is ownership. The key quote being "nobody being able to take personal control of resources" which is clearly not the current system, wherein private citizens own and control virtually all resources. I don't think anyone can seriously suggest that mere regulation is enough to create a socialist system.

"beyond their own personal posessions"

Keep in mind this definition doesn't cover anything. It doesn't define what qualifies as a personal possession and what qualifies as resources. Like the video says, there are different types and ranges of socialism. In the US, resources controlled are services like infrastructure, Healthcare, and welfare.

But again, by that definition every government is socialist. What this video is attempting to describe is that there is a wide range of possible control that a government can exert over its economy: at one end of the scale is a free market, and at the other end is central planning.

Socialism is at one end of the scale; it is not itself the entire scale. Calling 99% of all possible governmental ideologies socialism is just silly; I may as well have made a video 30 years ago about "5 ways the USSR is already capitalist."
